title: Taiwan Should Be Kept Off the Negotiating Table
author: Allen Carlson
text:
U.S. President Trump delivers remarks to the press ahead of a summit meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the White House, Sep. 24, 2026.
Credit: Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok
The much-heralded China-U.S. summit is now behind us, and the consensus is that it produced nothing of substance. President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extended their trade truce, talked about artificial intelligence, and agreed on little else. Many have applied the same measure to Taiwan: Xi pressed Trump to shift American policy on the island, the American leader appears not to have obliged, and so, the reasoning goes, the U.S. position held and nothing happened. That reading is wrong. What looks like nothing is the clearest sign yet of how far the U.S. position on Taiwan has shifted. And Trump is solely responsible for such a change.[...]
